correctness.rationale: For every odd integer n>=3, maximal cliques of row, column or diagonal lines x=a,y=b,x+y=c are full n-vertex line simplices; any other clique is a mixed triangle indexed by (x,y,a≠0), total n²(n−1), because a fourth adjacent vertex forces 2a=0 and odd n excludes it. The line-core nerve has 3n line vertices, n² triangles each with free row-column edge, so collapses to a graph. Standard periodic triangular torus T_n embeds its 1-skeleton; every clique edge lies in a contractible line simplex and is endpoint-homotopic to torus unit edges, yielding π1(T_n) ->> π1(X_n). The two torus generators bound horizontal and vertical line-simplex disks; hence π1(X_n)=0. Counting Euler of line cover by inclusion-exclusion gives χ(Y)=3n−2n²; mixed triangles contribute n²(n−1), so χ(X)=1+(n−1)^3. The two-dimensional CW model and simple connectivity yield free H2 of that rank, then Hurewicz/Whitehead gives wedge of (n−1)^3 S². Independent maximal-clique enumeration for n=3,5,7 verified line/mixed decomposition and Euler; no extrapolation from these finite values is used.
